# 0005: Timeout order S3 60 s < ALB 120 s < Tomcat 130 s

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-16
- **Modules:** upload-service, local
- **Source:** design doc, section "ALB idle timeout and pod keep-alive" (linked from README.md in this folder)

## Decision

S3 write deadline 60 s < ALB idle timeout 120 s < Tomcat keep-alive 130 s. The service always answers before the ALB
gives up, and the ALB always closes idle connections before the pod does. The numbers are an estimate to adjust once
upload durations are measured.

## Rules for agents

Change these three values together, keeping the order S3 < ALB < Tomcat.

# Default settings for the upload service. device-logs.aws.region and device-logs.storage.bucket
# have no default here. Each environment sets them in cloud8-config-service-backend, and the app
# does not start without them.
#
# Still to add:
# - server.tomcat.keep-alive-timeout: 130 s (longer than the ALB idle timeout of 120 s).
# - server.shutdown: graceful.
# - device-logs.* defaults: rate limit 30 per 10 min, in-flight cap 200.
server:
  port: 1296
  # Stops Tomcat's RemoteIpValve, which Spring Boot adds on Kubernetes, from moving the ALB's
  # X-Forwarded-For entry into getRemoteAddr() before AlbHeaderTrust reads it (ADR 0004).
  # Don't override this or cloud8.config.forwarded-headers in cloud8-config-service-backend.
  forward-headers-strategy: none
spring:
  mvc:
    formcontent:
      filter:
        # Stops FormContentFilter reading a PUT body sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded before
        # the checks run, which would also make Tomcat send 100 Continue (ADR 0009).
        enabled: false
  servlet:
    multipart:
      # Stops DispatcherServlet parsing a multipart/* body before it picks the handler, for the same
      # reason. Phones never send multipart.
      enabled: false
management:
  server:
    port: 1297
device-logs:
  # The names AWS gives the headers the ALB adds after the mTLS handshake.
  trust:
    subject: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Subject
    issuer: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Issuer
    validity: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Validity
    serial-number: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Serial-Number
    leaf: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Leaf
    forwarded-for: X-Forwarded-For
  # One entry per contract FileType, or the app does not start. A disabled type gets 403, and a
  # Content-Length above max-size gets 413.
  file-types:
    app-log:
      enabled: true
      max-size: 10MB
    boot-log:
      enabled: true
      max-size: 10MB
    # Personal data. Stays off until the privacy review says yes (ADR 0008).
    calls-xml:
      enabled: false
      max-size: 10MB
  storage:
    # Below the ALB idle timeout of 120 s, so the phone hears 429 from the service instead of a
    # timeout from the ALB. Change it together with the ALB and Tomcat values (ADR 0005).
    write-timeout: 60s
cloud8:
  config:
    # Stops cloud8's ForwardedHeaderFilter from removing X-Forwarded-For before AlbHeaderTrust
    # reads it (ADR 0004).
    forwarded-headers:
      enabled: false
  security:
    # Replaces cloud8's /public/** default, so it is listed again. cloud8 turns CSRF off for
    # every public path, and phones carry no JWT.
    public-paths:
      - /public/**
      - /logs/**

50	## Why each choice
51	
52	- Defensive header parsing, and the Spring and cloud8 forwarded-header filters turned off: ADR 0004.
53	- Specific status codes, Content-Length required, never 503, every check before 100 Continue: ADR 0009.
54	- Timeout order S3 60 s < ALB 120 s < Tomcat 130 s, so the phone always hears us and not the ALB: ADR 0005.
55	- The key with no suffix and the create-only write: ADR 0011.
56	- `/logs/**` as a cloud8 public path, everything else still 401: ADR 0006.
57	- Per-pod in-memory rate limit behind an interface: ADR 0010.
58	- calls.xml off until the privacy review: ADR 0008.
59	- The ALB through the common chart ingress, the DigiCert certificate, the TLS policy: ADR 0001, 0002, 0003.
60	- Pod Identity for the S3 role, AWS SDK v2, the herd-endpoints namespace: ADR 0012, 0013, 0015.
61	
62	## What is deliberately not here
63	
64	Customer lookup, parsing and indexing belong to the processor, so a slow lookup can never delay or fail an upload.
65	There is no read API in this repo.
66

70	  `serviceaccount.yaml` with no role annotation (Pod Identity). `networkpolicy.yaml`: app port from the ALB's subnets
71	  only, since anything else in the VPC could send forged mTLS headers; management port from monitoring.
72	- Probes on `/public/ping`; the ALB health check on the same path. Readiness does not depend on S3, so an S3 blip does
73	  not drain every pod at once.
74	- Shutdown: `server.shutdown: graceful`, a preStop pause covering ALB deregistration, and a termination grace period
75	  longer than the slowest expected upload (start at 150 s).
76	- Scale: at least 3 replicas across zones, HPA on CPU. Uploads are I/O bound, so threads matter more than CPU; the
77	  designed in-flight cap protects each pod.

80

- `storage`: `LogStorage.store(LogObject)` returns `StoreResult.STORED` or `KEY_EXISTS`. `storage.s3.S3LogStorage` is
  the only implementation; tests use `InMemoryLogStorage`.
- `config`: `DeviceLogsProperties`, one record per group, refuses to start without an entry per `FileType`.
- `metrics`: `UploadMetrics`, the only place meters are created. A placeholder today.

## Why each choice

- Defensive header parsing, and the Spring and cloud8 forwarded-header filters turned off: ADR 0004.
- Specific status codes, Content-Length required, never 503, every check before 100 Continue: ADR 0009.
- Timeout order S3 60 s < ALB 120 s < Tomcat 130 s, so the phone always hears us and not the ALB: ADR 0005.
- The key with no suffix and the create-only write: ADR 0011.
- `/logs/**` as a cloud8 public path, everything else still 401: ADR 0006.
- Per-pod in-memory rate limit behind an interface: ADR 0010.
- calls.xml off until the privacy review: ADR 0008.
- The ALB through the common chart ingress, the DigiCert certificate, the TLS policy: ADR 0001, 0002, 0003.
- Pod Identity for the S3 role, AWS SDK v2, the herd-endpoints namespace: ADR 0012, 0013, 0015.

## What is deliberately not here

Customer lookup, parsing and indexing belong to the processor, so a slow lookup can never delay or fail an upload.
There is no read API in this repo.

## Runtime (designed; the chart is a placeholder)

- Chart `device-log-upload-service-chart` on cloud8-common-chart. Ingress from the common chart with class `alb`.
  `serviceaccount.yaml` with no role annotation (Pod Identity). `networkpolicy.yaml`: app port from the ALB's subnets
  only, since anything else in the VPC could send forged mTLS headers; management port from monitoring.
- Probes on `/public/ping`; the ALB health check on the same path. Readiness does not depend on S3, so an S3 blip does
  not drain every pod at once.
- Shutdown: `server.shutdown: graceful`, a preStop pause covering ALB deregistration, and a termination grace period
  longer than the slowest expected upload (start at 150 s).
- Scale: at least 3 replicas across zones, HPA on CPU. Uploads are I/O bound, so threads matter more than CPU; the
  designed in-flight cap protects each pod.

## Status against the design

Built: the request path above, the status codes, streaming, the create-only write, the structured log line. Not built:
the rate limit and in-flight cap, metrics, the keep-alive and graceful-shutdown settings, the Helm chart, and the file
types beyond app.log, boot.log and calls.xml. Each gap is also noted in the ADR it belongs to.

file.content:
# upload-service configuration

Every `device-logs.*` setting is a field of `config/DeviceLogsProperties.java`, validated at startup, so a missing or
invalid value stops the pod before it serves traffic. Defaults live in `src/main/resources/application.yml`; each
environment overrides them in cloud8-config-service-backend; `application-local-test.yml` holds the LocalStack values.
If this table and the code disagree, the code is right. Change both in the same PR.

## Settings

| Setting | Default in the repo | Set per environment | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device-logs.aws.region` | none, required | config backend | |
| `device-logs.aws.endpoint-override` | empty | `local-test` only | LocalStack URL. Empty in AWS. |
| `device-logs.storage.bucket` | none, required | config backend | One bucket per deployment, for data residency. |
| `device-logs.storage.write-timeout` | 60 s | config backend | Deadline for one S3 write, body included. Must stay below the ALB idle timeout (ADR 0005). |
| `device-logs.file-types.<type>.enabled` | app-log true, boot-log true, calls-xml false | config backend | One entry per contract `FileType` or the app does not start. A disabled type gets 403 (ADR 0007, ADR 0008). |
| `device-logs.file-types.<type>.max-size` | 10MB each | config backend | A larger Content-Length gets 413. |
| `device-logs.trust.subject`, `.issuer`, `.validity`, `.serial-number`, `.leaf` | AWS default `X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-*` names | config backend, if the ALB renames them | Only `trust/AlbHeaderTrust` reads them (ADR 0004). |
| `device-logs.trust.forwarded-for` | `X-Forwarded-For` | config backend | The last entry is the source IP. |

## Fixed in application.yml, not per environment

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `server.port`, `management.server.port` | 1296, 1297 | |
| `server.forward-headers-strategy` | none | Keeps Tomcat's RemoteIpValve from rewriting the ALB headers before `AlbHeaderTrust` reads them (ADR 0004). Do not override. |
| `cloud8.config.forwarded-headers.enabled` | false | Same reason, for cloud8's filter (ADR 0004). Do not override. |
| `spring.mvc.formcontent.filter.enabled`, `spring.servlet.multipart.enabled` | false | Nothing may read the body before the checks run (ADR 0009). |
| `cloud8.security.public-paths` | `/public/**`, `/logs/**` | Phones carry no JWT (ADR 0006). The list replaces cloud8's default, so `/public/**` is listed again. |

## Designed, not in the code yet

| Setting | Planned default | Record |
|---|---|---|
| `device-logs.rate-limit.per-mac.capacity`, `.refill-period` | 30 per 10 min | ADR 0010 |
| `device-logs.inflight.max-per-pod` | 200 | design doc, Configuration |
| `server.tomcat.keep-alive-timeout` | 130 s | ADR 0005 |
| `server.shutdown` | graceful | design doc, Helm, ALB and runtime |

## Helm values, set per cluster in GDS

Role ARN is not one: Pod Identity binds the role by service account name (ADR 0012). The ingress annotations
(certificate ARN, trust store ARN, hostname, TLS policy, idle timeout), replicas and resources are placeholders in
`src/main/helm/device-log-upload-service-chart/values.yaml` and filled in per cluster. The chart is a placeholder today.

content.text:
You can't change the S3 value on its own. ADR 0005 requires the order **S3 write < ALB idle < Tomcat keep-alive**, and those three change together. 150 s is already above the ALB's 120 s, so the ALB and Tomcat values have to go up too. ADR 0005's title and Decision name the exact numbers (60/120/130), so this needs a new ADR that supersedes 0005. Per CLAUDE.md, that means a person decides first.

## What has to change and where each value is set

| Value | Today | Where it's set |
|---|---|---|
| S3 write deadline | 60 s | `upload-service/src/main/resources/application.yml:55` (`device-logs.storage.write-timeout`), overridable per environment in cloud8-config-service-backend. It reaches the SDK as `apiCallTimeout` in `storage/s3/S3ClientConfig.java:30`. |
| ALB idle timeout (must become > 150 s) | 120 s | An ingress annotation in `upload-service/src/main/helm/device-log-upload-service-chart/values.yaml`. That file is only a placeholder comment today, and the value is set per cluster in GDS. |
| Tomcat keep-alive (must become > the new ALB value) | 130 s, planned | Not built yet. It's listed under "Designed, not in the code yet" in `upload-service/CONFIGURATION.md:37` and as a "Still to add" item in `application.yml:6`. |
| Pod termination grace period | 150 s, planned | `values.yaml` (placeholder). `ARCHITECTURE.md:74-75` says it must be longer than the slowest upload, so 150 s is no longer enough. |
| Local Envoy (stands in for the ALB) | 120 s | `local/envoy/envoy.yaml:47,49,115` (`stream_idle_timeout`, `idle_timeout`) |

**Docs and tests that mention 60 s:**
- The Javadoc in `DeviceLogsProperties.java:71-72`
- The row in `upload-service/CONFIGURATION.md:15`
- The `STORAGE_FAILED` description in `openapi.yaml:119`
- The comments in `envoy.yaml:69-71` and `local/CLAUDE.md:59`
- `upload-service/ARCHITECTURE.md:54`
- Tests: `S3ClientConfigTest.java:42` asserts 60 s, and `DeviceLogsPropertiesTest.java:86` (`...WithA60sDeadline`) needs its name and value updated.

`docs/load-tests/README.md:32` says to run the load tests before any timeout change.

## What goes wrong if only the S3 value changes

- **The ALB times out before the service answers.** Once the body has arrived, nothing crosses the connection while the S3 write runs. Any write that takes between 120 s and 150 s hits the ALB's idle timeout first. The phone gets a timeout from the ALB instead of the service's 429, which is the exact case ADR 0005 exists to prevent. Locally, Envoy's 120 s idle timeout does the same.
- **The phone can't tell whether the upload worked.** S3 can still commit the object after the connection is cut (`openapi.yaml:119`, `LogStorage.java:18-19`), so a failure the phone sees may actually have been stored.
- **Shutdown can cut off uploads.** A 150 s grace period no longer covers a 150 s write plus the preStop pause, so a pod being shut down can kill uploads still in progress.
- **The service and the ALB fall out of step on idle connections.** If the ALB is raised later but Tomcat's keep-alive isn't raised above it, the pod closes idle connections before the ALB does. That breaks the second half of ADR 0005.

## Needs a person

- The new ALB idle and grace-period values are GDS values, and the environment's write-timeout lives in the config backend. Neither is in this repo, so someone has to set them.
- The new ADR has to be approved before any of this changes.

## Files used

- `docs/architecture/decisions/0005-timeout-order.md`
- `upload-service/src/main/resources/application.yml`
- `upload-service/CONFIGURATION.md`
- `upload-service/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `upload-service/CLAUDE.md`
- `upload-service/openapi.yaml`
- `upload-service/src/main/helm/device-log-upload-service-chart/values.yaml`
- `upload-service/src/main/java/.../config/DeviceLogsProperties.java`
- `upload-service/src/main/java/.../storage/s3/S3ClientConfig.java`
- `upload-service/src/main/java/.../storage/LogStorage.java`
- `upload-service/src/test/java/.../storage/s3/S3ClientConfigTest.java`
- `upload-service/src/test/java/.../config/DeviceLogsPropertiesTest.java`
- `local/envoy/envoy.yaml`
- `local/CLAUDE.md`
- `docs/load-tests/README.md`
- `CLAUDE.md`

## What goes wrong if only the S3 value changes

- **The ALB times out before the service answers.** Once the body has arrived, nothing crosses the connection while the S3 write runs. Any write that takes between 120 s and 150 s hits the ALB's idle timeout first. The phone gets a timeout from the ALB instead of the service's 429, which is the exact case ADR 0005 exists to prevent. Locally, Envoy's 120 s idle timeout does the same.
- **The phone can't tell whether the upload worked.** S3 can still commit the object after the connection is cut (`openapi.yaml:119`, `LogStorage.java:18-19`), so a failure the phone sees may actually have been stored.
- **Shutdown can cut off uploads.** A 150 s grace period no longer covers a 150 s write plus the preStop pause, so a pod being shut down can kill uploads still in progress.
- **The service and the ALB fall out of step on idle connections.** If the ALB is raised later but Tomcat's keep-alive isn't raised above it, the pod closes idle connections before the ALB does. That breaks the second half of ADR 0005.

## Needs a person

- The new ALB idle and grace-period values are GDS values, and the environment's write-timeout lives in the config backend. Neither is in this repo, so someone has to set them.
- The new ADR has to be approved before any of this changes.
